title: Signature Inverted index construction — Keyword Search
description: Signature original — The inverted index is the core data structure of keyword search: a dictionary mapping every distinct term to the sorted list of document identifiers that contain it, called a postings list. It is built by tokenizing each document, normalizing case and punctuation, then appending the document id to each term's postings list, finishing with a sort and dedupe pass. Queries then run in time proportional to postings length instead of corpus size, which is why full-text engines answer in milliseconds over millions of documents. title: Signature Tokenization and normalization — Keyword Search
description: Signature original — Tokenization splits raw text into searchable terms, deciding where word boundaries fall across whitespace, punctuation, hyphens, and apostrophes. Normalization then folds case, strips diacritics where appropriate, and removes surrounding punctuation so that 'Archive', 'archive,' and 'ARCHIVE' all match the same postings list. Consistent tokenization at index time and query time is what makes keyword search reliable; mismatched rules are the most common cause of missed hits. title: Signature Boolean AND over postings — Keyword Search
description: Signature original — A multi-term keyword query with AND semantics is answered by intersecting the postings lists of its terms. Because each postings list is sorted by document id, intersection runs as a linear two-pointer merge that advances the lagging pointer until ids align or one list is exhausted. This merge costs O(x + y) for lists of length x and y, and it scales to many terms by intersecting the shortest lists first. title: Signature Boolean OR over postings — Keyword Search
description: Signature original — OR semantics are answered by unioning postings lists, again with a linear merge over the sorted id sequences. The union walk emits each document id once even when it appears in several lists, preserving the sorted order of the result. Union cost is linear in the total postings length, which is why very common terms dominate OR query time. title: Signature Phrase search with positions — Keyword Search
description: Signature original — A positional index stores not just which documents contain a term but the word offsets where it occurs. A phrase query like "climate archive" then requires the postings of 'climate' and 'archive' to share a document with offsets differing by exactly one. Positions roughly double index size but unlock exact-phrase and proximity matching that plain postings cannot express. title: Signature TF-IDF ranking — Keyword Search
description: Signature original — When many documents match, TF-IDF ranks them: term frequency (how often the term occurs in the document) multiplied by inverse document frequency (how rare the term is across the corpus). Rare query terms therefore contribute more score than common ones, pushing the most distinctive matches to the top. TF-IDF needs only index statistics, no training, and remains the baseline every learned ranker is compared against. title: Signature Stop-word removal — Keyword Search
description: Signature original — Stop words are high-frequency, low-signal terms such as 'the', 'and', and 'of' that appear in nearly every document. Removing them at index time shrinks the index and speeds queries, at the cost of breaking exact phrases that contain them. Modern engines often keep stop words in positional indexes instead, trading space for phrase fidelity. title: Signature Stemming with suffix rules — Keyword Search
description: Signature original — Stemming conflates morphological variants by stripping suffixes, so 'archives', 'archived', and 'archiving' all index under 'archiv'. Rule-based stemmers apply ordered rewrite rules (plurals, -ing, -ed, -tion) with guards against over-stripping short stems. Stemming raises recall for inflected languages but can merge unrelated words, which is why some systems index both stemmed and unstemmed forms. title: Signature Proximity search (NEAR/n) — Keyword Search
description: Signature original — Proximity search generalizes phrase search: two terms match when their positional offsets differ by at most n, in either order. The engine walks both position lists with two pointers, recording document ids where any pair of positions falls inside the window. NEAR queries capture paraphrases that exact phrases miss, at a modest extra cost over phrase evaluation. title: Signature Wildcard expansion — Keyword Search
description: Signature original — A trailing wildcard like 'archiv*' is expanded by walking a prefix trie of the vocabulary to collect every term with that prefix. The query then becomes an OR over the expanded term set, evaluated with the standard union merge. Expansion is bounded in practice by limiting the number of expanded terms or requiring a minimum prefix length. title: Signature Fielded search — Keyword Search
description: Signature original — Fielded search restricts terms to document fields, as in 'title:archive' versus 'body:archive'. The index stores separate postings per field, or tags each posting with its field, so the query planner can intersect within the requested field only. Fields let ranking weight title matches above body matches, a standard precision booster. title: Signature Index compression — Keyword Search
description: Signature original — Postings lists compress well because sorted document ids become small gaps; gap encoding stores differences instead of raw ids. Variable-byte or Elias codes then store small gaps in fewer bytes, often shrinking indexes to a third of their raw size. Smaller indexes mean more of the hot postings fit in memory, which directly cuts query latency. title: Signature Incremental index updates — Keyword Search
description: Signature original — Large indexes avoid full rebuilds by buffering new documents in a small in-memory segment that is searched alongside the main index. Periodically the segments merge in a background pass that rewrites postings lists in sorted order. This log-structured approach keeps ingest fast while queries simply union results across segments. title: Signature Query parsing and precedence — Keyword Search
description: Signature original — A query parser turns user text into an execution plan, honoring the precedence NOT > AND > OR and explicit parentheses. The classic shunting-yard algorithm converts the infix expression to postfix, which a stack machine then evaluates against postings lists. Correct precedence handling is what makes '(a OR b) AND NOT c' behave the way users expect. title: Signature Result snippet generation — Keyword Search
description: Signature original — Snippets show each hit in context: the engine locates query-term positions in the document and cuts a window of surrounding words. Overlapping windows merge, query terms get highlighted, and the most term-dense window wins when space is limited. Good snippets let users judge relevance without opening the document, cutting wasted clicks.
